title: Duplicated Sequential Write-Back Logic
pattern: Manually coding direct update queries to database tables inside every business transaction script or endpoint.
why_bad: Knowledge of database change tracking is scattered. If an endpoint fails to manually save a modified nested record, the database becomes corrupt and inconsistent.
detection: Repeated manual SQL update statements or transactional sequential saves written within separate controller methods.
fix: Use a Unit of Work pattern to track in-memory entity changes automatically and perform a single, atomic flush.
source: *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture*, "Unit of Work", p. 184.
